bull_bear.body: **100% payout of FY26 profit (Rs.9,825 cr)** via hybrid base-dividend + buyback (buyback concluded last week; ~Rs.10,000 cr total to shareholders in July — buyback route chosen for post-Finance-Act tax attractiveness to non-promoters). Cash to dip from >Rs.21,000 cr then rebuild to ~Rs.15,000 cr target by FY27-end on ~80% cash conversion.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Commodity super-cycle broadening** into components/electronics/labour/logistics/energy — Q2 to feel fuller impact; pricing is "one lever, not the only one."
- **Currency dependence:** margin cushion hinges on a weak rupee; RBI measures could reverse it.
- **Operational fragility exposed:** ransomware shutdown + LPG/fuel curtailment + West-Asia force-majeure + election-driven labour shortage cost ~10% volume this quarter — recurrence risk.
- **Bottom-of-pyramid weakness:** 100cc/125cc growing low-single-digit; Bajaj ceding 100cc share by choice (profitability over volume) → wholesale market share drifting down.
- KTM comparability/normalization over coming quarters; consol optics inflated by consolidation.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, granular, strategically candid. Rakesh Sharma frank on trade-offs ("participate in 100cc on our own terms… prepared to lose market share"; "we will not buy market share"). Dinesh Thapar disciplined and specific on the inflation bridge and capital return. Playful but precise ("you guys are not taking me seriously… 10 models in 6 weeks"). Proactively returned to an unanswered EV-profitability question at close.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Reported records **understate** underlying: ~10% volume was lost to one-off shocks — true run-rate was tracking >1.5m units.
- EV surge (+67-70%) is being driven by petrol-price fear post West-Asia crisis and is **cannibalizing ICE scooters specifically** (range parity with scooters, not motorcycles) — a demand-mix, not just subsidy, story.
- Consol growth flatters via KTM full-quarter consolidation — watch standalone + BACL for clean signal; BACL AUM Rs.20,000 cr (+70%), ROE >25% is a quietly large financing engine.
- 100% FY26 payout + buyback signals capital-return discipline while still funding a 25% capacity build — cash machine funding both.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- World's largest three-wheeler manufacturer and India's largest exporter of two- and three-wheelers, with presence in over 100 countries and over 32 million vehicles sold historically.
- Domestic ICE three-wheeler market leadership with 73.8% overall share (79.1% passenger carriers, 52.5% goods carriers) and 87.9% share in CNG three-wheelers.
- Export distribution strength: No.1 position in 9 of 15 key motorcycle export markets and leadership in 11 of 12 key commercial-vehicle export markets.
- Premium brand portfolio (Pulsar, KTM, Triumph) sustained by continuous product refresh cadence and R&D investment -- reorganised R&D with expanded design/analysis/validation teams and a growing IP portfolio (patent filings across Powertrain, Vehicle and Integration domains).
- Early-mover position in electric mobility: India's largest combined electric 2W+3W player, with Chetak among the top-two electric scooter brands (20.7% share) and pole position in the E3W (L5) segment achieved within three years of entry.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Erosion of domestic motorcycle market share amid heightened competitive intensity — Bajaj Auto's domestic motorcycle market share declined from 16.6% in FY2025 to 15.6% in FY2026 (BAL's own volumes grew only 0.6% versus 6.6% industry growth), driven by heightened competitive intensity particularly in the entry and mid-commuter categories.
- Rare-earth magnet supply-chain vulnerability — Non-availability of rare earth magnets, a consequence of Chinese export restrictions, disrupted Chetak (EV) supply in H1 FY2026 and constrained volumes even as demand remained strong; management explicitly cites this as a supply-chain risk the company encountered during the year, remedied via alternate motor designs and alternate geographic sourcing.
- Geopolitical and regulatory/macro-economic risk in export markets — Management's Risk & Opportunities section explicitly flags geopolitical tensions and evolving regulatory and macroeconomic conditions in export markets as a dynamic risk requiring continuous scanning, relevant given the Company's substantial reliance on international/export revenue.
- Commodity cost inflation / margin pressure — Management states it 'remains mindful of margin pressures arising from an increasing commodity pressure' going into the coming year, and that balancing growth and profitability against this will be a key operational task.
- Currency volatility — Currency volatility is explicitly named among the dynamic external risks scanned under the Company's Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework; FY2026 margins benefited from favourable USD/INR realisation, indicating margin sensitivity could reverse with currency moves.
- Technological disruption — Technological disruption is explicitly named as a risk category management continuously scans and anticipates under its ERM framework, relevant to the Company's ongoing ICE-to-EV transition across two- and three-wheelers.
- KTM AG turnaround execution risk — Bajaj Auto acquired a controlling stake in KTM AG following the group's self-administration/restructuring proceedings in Austria; management states the turnaround is 'well underway' but not yet complete, with the aim to restore KTM to its original performance levels 'in due course' -- an unresolved execution risk on a newly-controlled, previously-distressed subsidiary.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

- **KTM AG:** first full quarter of consolidation; turnaround "in line with roadmap" — production ramped, inventories normalized, fixed-cost control showing.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Deepen competitiveness in the strategically important 125cc+ motorcycle segment through pricing and product interventions, including the Pulsar portfolio revamp and expansion.
- Sustain and build market leadership in electric three-wheelers under the WEGO brand, with the longer-term intent of mirroring the scale of leadership achieved in the ICE three-wheeler category.
- Scale up Chetak through recent product launches (e.g. Chetak C25) to grow market share in the electric two-wheeler segment.
- Sustain export momentum, supported by improving macro-economic conditions across key international markets.
- Nurture and expand the premium global portfolios under KTM and Triumph to further strengthen international market positioning.
- Support KTM AG's turnaround for the coming year through portfolio prioritisation, product development, go-to-market execution, supply chain optimisation and organisational simplification, aiming to restore KTM to its original performance levels.
- Build capability and leverage scale in Bajaj Auto Credit (BACL) to deliver an industry-class-leading financing performance.
- Balance growth and profitability through robust operational management, mindful of margin pressure from rising commodity costs.
- Operate a robust Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework to proactively scan, anticipate and convert emerging risks (geopolitical, regulatory, commodity, supply-chain, currency, technological) into strategic advantage.
- The Company follows a formal Dividend Distribution Policy (regulation 43A of SEBI LODR) governing the parameters and circumstances the Board considers in determining dividend distribution, framed around a stated commitment to 'consistently reward its shareholders and deliver sustainable returns' commensurate with growth and performance. For FY2026, to mark the Bajaj Group's centenary year and Bajaj Auto's position as flagship company, the Board approved a one-off combined payout (dividend + share buyback via tender offer) equivalent to 100% of the year's profit after tax. Outside of that payout, the Board elected to retain the entire remaining profit for the year in distributable retained earnings (i.e., no separate transfer to general reserve). The Company maintains a policy of funding capex and strategic investments (e.g., in Bajaj Auto Credit, Bajaj Auto Technology, and the KTM restructuring) out of internal cash generation while preserving a healthy, surplus-cash balance sheet; it has not issued debt instruments or undertaken fixed deposit programmes and holds top-tier domestic credit ratings for its bank facilities.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY2026 Bajaj Auto invested ~Rs 500 crore in capex and Rs 2,300+ crore in strategic bets (Bajaj Auto Credit Ltd. and Bajaj Auto International Holdings BV), funded from surplus cash generation, alongside meaningful investment across strategic priorities: growing its electric-mobility presence, scaling the Bajaj Auto Credit financing business, sharpening R&D capability through Bajaj Auto Technology Ltd., acquiring and assuming control over the KTM group, and widening its portfolio/footprint to capture domestic and international growth opportunities. The Directors' Report states the Company's current installed capacity at 7.2 million units per annum. Distribution/retail footprint expansion during the year included: 80 operational 'KT Showrooms' -- a new joint KTM-Triumph retail format; over 500 exclusive Chetak Experience Centres and more than 4,000 Chetak touchpoints; and, at the Brazil subsidiary (Bajaj Do Brasil), a manufacturing capacity ramp-up to 50,000 units per annum together with dealership network expansion to over 60 dealerships across 24 states. On the product/technology side, R&D was reorganised with expanded design, analysis and validation teams, several new test and prototyping facilities were added, and the IP portfolio grew via patent filings across Powertrain, Vehicle and Integration domains. Per BRSR Principle 2 disclosures, 55.9% of capex investment during FY2026 was directed to technologies with environmental/social benefit, specifically named as: 2-wheeler Chetak assembly and paint shop, 3-wheeler EV vehicle assembly, and dies and moulds. Bajaj Auto Technology Ltd. also developed alternate motor designs using light rare-earth magnets and established alternate geographic sourcing to restore Chetak supply after H1 disruption from Chinese rare-earth export restrictions.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- GST rationalisation in September 2025 (motorcycle rate up to 350cc cut from 28% to 18%) triggered a brief pre-cut pause followed by sharp H2 acceleration and record festive-season retail.
- Domestic motorcycle industry grew 6.6% in FY2026 to ~13.1 million units (highest since FY2019), but the year was split into a flat/declining H1 and a strong double-digit H2.
- 125cc+ premiumisation is a structural driver, now 77.5% of total motorcycle sales, amid heightened competitive intensity in entry and mid-commuter categories.
- Export recovery is a key driver: monthly export volumes crossed 2 lakh units in October 2025 for the first time in 39 months; LATAM delivered its best-ever year; East Africa and South Asia were the biggest growth drivers.
- Margin improvement (EBITDA margin 20.5%, +30 bps YoY) driven by favourable USD/INR realisation, a profitable mix and operating leverage, which more than offset the margin-dilutive scale-up of electric two-wheeler sales and continued competitive investment.
- Chetak volumes were constrained in H1 by non-availability of rare-earth magnets following Chinese export restrictions; supply was restored by end-September 2025 via alternate motor designs and alternate geographic sourcing, enabling a strong H2 recovery.
- Resilient Indian macro backdrop -- GDP growth moderating to 6.5% (IMF) with private consumption near 56% of GDP, benign inflation enabling RBI rate cuts (repo rate to 5.25% by April 2026) -- supports domestic demand.
- Management flags continuing margin pressure ahead from increasing commodity cost inflation, to be managed through disciplined operational execution.

deepdive.thesis: Record quarter on every line (vol 1.4m +29%, rev Rs.17,244 cr +37%, EBITDA Rs.3,596 cr +45%, PAT ~Rs.3,000 cr +42%) delivered *through* a hyperinflationary commodity shock (~4.5% of revenue), a ransomware shutdown and West-Asia supply disruptions that cost ~10% of volume. Margin still expanded to 20.9% (+110 bps YoY) on currency (USD-INR 94.4), mix and cost discipline. Exports (40% of rev) and EV (now 30% of domestic rev, double-digit EBITDA, Chetak turned EBITDA-positive) are the twin growth engines; capacity is now the binding constraint → 7m→9m units expansion underway.

verdicts.item: Intend to launch a modern e-Rick by end of FY25 (may spill into first week of April), entering a segment of over 40,000-45,000 units/month.
verdicts.note: 'On Riki, our E-Rick, the journey is progressing steadily with presence now in 100-plus cities'

verdicts.item: Expect L5 3-wheeler industry to grow at 4% to 6%, primarily driven by increasing EV penetration; expect to outpace industry EV growth while maintaining ICE leadership.
verdicts.note: 'We have maintained the number 1 position in electric 3-wheelers throughout Q4 and in April' — outpacing on EV; FY26 industry grew [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Expect a major swing into profitability zone for Chetak in Q4FY25 as the new 35-Series acquires scale beginning February; new Chetak model has line of sight on EBITDA breakeven.
verdicts.note: EV portfolio 'contributing double-digit EBITDA percentage'; Chetak scaled to 5 lakh units — profitability swing realized

verdicts.item: KTM is of strategic importance and Bajaj remains strongly committed; financial considerations to play out over next ~4 weeks (restructuring package deadline 25 February).
verdicts.note: 'the transaction completed on 18th of November, Bajaj moved from being a minority position to a controlling stake'

verdicts.item: Expect real scale-up of e-rick to commence in Q1FY26; aim to organize the fragmented ~45,000/month e-rick market and bring new business.
verdicts.note: 'presence now in 100-plus cities ... the E-Rick segment itself has slowed down due to enforcement of regulation' — partial scale-up amid headwind

wtt.summary: 57% guidance hit (22 chains); 7/8 projects on-time; 2 expired; 19% theme consistency (info)

meta.thesis: Record quarter on every line (vol 1.4m +29%, rev Rs.17,244 cr +37%, EBITDA Rs.3,596 cr +45%, PAT ~Rs.3,000 cr +42%) delivered *through* a hyperinflationary commodity shock (~4.5% of revenue), a ransomware shutdown and West-Asia supply disruptions that cost ~10% of volume. Margin still expanded to 20.9% (+110 bps YoY) on currency (USD-INR 94.4), mix and cost discipline. Exports (40% of rev) and EV (now 30% of domestic rev, double-digit EBITDA, Chetak turned EBITDA-positive) are the twin growth engines; capacity is now the binding constraint → 7m→9m units expansion underway.
